newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica to use cash-flow to reduce debt.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica to use cash-flow to reduce debt.

text.p: The chairman of Spain's Telefonica de Espana said on Tuesday the group, which is to be fully privatised on February 18, was eager to clean up its balance sheet and would use increasing cash-flow to reduce debt levels.

"We would like to get a more solid balance-sheet," Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga said at a presentation of the share offer at Madrid's bourse. "We are reducing the level of debt by improving the cash-flow of the group."

Demand for Telefonica shares on Monday, the first day of the offer of the state's remaining 20.9 percent stake, was very heavy with some 90,000 new, individual investors signing up for the retail tranche.
Analysts say that the institutional demand will be weaker with those investors more wary of Telefonica's high debt levels in comparison with most other European telecoms.

Villalonga said the group's debt to share capital ratio would be cut by 40 percent by the year 2000, bringing it more in line the rest of Europe. In addition, he said the company was aiming to increase its level of self-financing by 110 percent.

He said Telefonica's strategy as a fully-privatised operator would be four pronged: better customer service, maximum use of growth opportunities, increased efficiency, and reorganisation of the management structure toward a more centralised control.
"The primary message of this presentation is that we plan to maximize the value of the share for all shareholders," Villalonga said.
To that end, the group plans to increase productivity to 360 clients per employee by the year 2000 and increase the use of existing lines and new services through volume discounts and special offers.

Telefonica directors speaking at the presentation predicted that dividends would keep rising in line with the operator's policy to pay out a little bit more than the parent company profits and a little bit less than the group's profits.
